final.strategist: lead-synthesis (final). Spine: unit-economics draft (response curves with the 2025-measured paid beta, exact additive waterfall, projected-CPV gate). Grafts: show-up draft (sequential no-show order, leak-proof seat ops, commitment-ladder encouragement test, dated gates, person-week budget); community draft (club charters, Club Cup on verified check-ins, metro-corridor sequencing, 82% show-up ceiling); loops draft (k = share x invites x conversion, day-1 6 pm 'bring a friend tomorrow' link, GCC-interview ambassador rewards). Judge fixes applied: stall-fix double count removed from base; 10pp marginal-quality haircut; creator beta set to the measured paid beta; engine and leak fix sequenced so neither is counted twice; 10-12 h daytime hackathon; CPPMS permit for 5,000; identified-to-registered corrected to 80.0%; Shivaratri, Eid and first-year mid-term timing corrected. All numbers re-derived in a script; the waterfall reconciles exactly.
final.big_idea: Yes, this is Challenge A (Attendee Growth). Buy verified check-ins, not reach. Cut paid social and creators from Rs 1,52,000 to Rs 55,000: in 2025 the last Rs 40.2K of paid bought registrations at Rs 200 each, against Rs 110 for the first Rs 52.8K. Move that money into a 40-college club-charter grid, a check-in-paid peer loop and a sponsor-gated competition track. Then protect every registration with a WhatsApp 'reserved-for-you' engine and airline-style seat operations, because 300 of 2025's 875 registrant no-shows never even held a live pass. Result on the same Rs 3,00,000: 2,717 verified visitors in the base case (Rs 110 each, against Rs 134 in 2025) and 3,470 in the stretch (Rs 86 each). Nearly half of the base growth comes from people who had already registered.
final.north_star: Unique verified external visitors: distinct external people, deduplicated by stable ID (phone plus college-ID hash) across both days, whose QR check-in is both admitted and verified. These are the same rules that produced 2025's 2,050 [DS]. Input-metric tree [GRO-01]: (1) registrations by source, i.e. partner-code, squad-link, ambassador, competition and CTWA codes; (2) live-pass share at T-0 (2025: 89.3%; base 93.6%); (3) T-8 reconfirm rate by channel, the leading indicator that recalibrates the show-up forecast on Fri 5 Mar; (4) registrant show-up (2025: 68.8%; base 78.5%; ceiling 82% [SHOW-02]); (5) walk-ins, capped at 300 a day. Guardrails: projected cost per verified visitor of Rs 120 or less to scale (2025 blended: Rs 134); WhatsApp opt-out under 3%; forecast peak on site at no more than 90% of the 5,000 police permit. Registrations are an input, never the goal.

Tier-1 by rule and cheaper than its peers. Hyderabad (UA) is an X-class city under the 7th CPC HRA order [mkt HYD-24]. Mercer 2024 ranks Hyderabad 202, against Bengaluru 195, Delhi 164 and Mumbai 136 [mkt HYD-27], so in-kind and sponsor budgets stretch further.

A dense, clustered student market. Hyderabad district has 465 colleges (4th in India) and Ranga Reddy 338 (9th) [mkt HYD-04]. Telangana's GER is 46.6, against 30.0 for India [mkt HYD-02]. 107 of 175 engineering colleges (61%) sit in Hyderabad, Medchal-Malkajgiri and Ranga Reddy [mkt HYD-11], which is ideal for a partner grid, college buses and squads.

A tech-heavy audience with a natural sponsor base. 83,622 of 1,16,877 engineering seats (72%) are in CSE or allied branches [mkt HYD-09], and about 515 GCCs operate in the city [mkt HYD-26]. That supports a sponsor-funded AI hackathon and GCC internship-interview rewards.

Cheap local media and messaging. Reels CPM is Rs 45-140 against Rs 150-350 for Feed [PAID-01]. India's Meta CPM bottomed in February 2026 [PAID-03]. Hyderabad nano creators charge Rs 3-8K per Reel [INF-03]. A WhatsApp utility message costs Rs 0.115 [WA-01], and a Click-to-WhatsApp chat opens a free 7-day window [WA-03].

The market is not the constraint. The stretch target of 3,470 is 0.67% of the 5.2-lakh priority pool, so the binding limits are conversion, cost per visitor, team bandwidth and four known operating limits: the Cyberabad CPPMS permit [cal HYD-26], the 10 pm outdoor sound cut-off [cal HYD-27], the 11 pm last metro [cal HYD-11], and HITEX's distance of 2.6 km from HITEC City station [cal HYD-15].

A clean date. Sat-Sun 13-14 Mar 2027 falls after the JNTUH II-IV mid-terms (1-6 Feb) [cal HYD-01], after GATE (Feb weekends) [cal HYD-07], after the I-year mid-terms (3-9 Mar) [cal HYD-02] and after Eid (10 Mar) [cal HYD-04]. It falls before Holi (22 Mar) [cal HYD-05] and the April mid-terms, and after the Elan, Felicity and Pearl window (Jan-Feb) [fest HYD-01, HYD-04, HYD-07]. 13 Mar is a second Saturday, often a college holiday (to be verified per partner).

fest_dates_and_timeline.focus: Cleanest weekend: after every mid-term, GATE, Shivaratri (Sat 6 Mar) and Eid (Wed 10 Mar), and before Holi (22 Mar) [cal HYD-01/02/04/05/07]. Intermediate exams (24 Feb-20 Mar) [cal HYD-08] rule out Class 12 students. If the IPL fixtures (expected by mid-Feb) put an SRH home match at Uppal on 13-14 Mar [cal HYD-09], switch to 20-21 Mar. The pro-nite ends at 9:45 pm for the 10 pm sound rule, the 11 pm last metro and women students' travel.

Tracking stack: QR pass, partner, squad, ambassador and competition codes, UTMs, WhatsApp BSP, holdout randomiser. Growth Center wired to the 2027 tables by 15 Dec. Geocode the 107 metro engineering colleges and the large OU-area colleges into 6 corridor clusters, and shortlist 60 for matched-pair waves. Recruit 60 ambassadors (non-partner colleges only). Pitch competition sponsors. The venue (HITEX) and production sponsor are an out-of-scope dependency.

WhatsApp interest list opens 21 Dec, so identified leads build up before registration (median identified-to-registered lag is 7 days [DS]). 25 MoUs by Sun 10 Jan. Templates approved and flows built by 10 Jan. January club workshops at pilot colleges double as reminder test beds. Competition sponsor go/no-go Fri 15 Jan. Pushes stay quiet over Sankranti (13-17 Jan) [fest HYD-21]. Check autonomous-college calendars, e.g. NRCM mid-terms 25-30 Jan [cal HYD-03].

Registration opens Mon 18 Jan, 54 days out. Wave A: 20 partner colleges in the Kukatpally-Miyapur and Gandipet-Gachibowli corridors go live. CTWA pilot (Rs 12K) with a 3-lit / 2-dark cluster geo-lift test. Squad-first vs solo A/B. 15% reminder holdout randomised. Gate 1 on Sun 31 Jan: pacing target 20% of base registrations (660), plus squad k, Wave A activation and pilot CPR.

JNTUH mid-terms (1-6 Feb) and GATE (6-7 Feb). No campus pushes and no paid flights; only the WhatsApp engine runs. Gate 2 on Sun 7 Feb: pacing 30% (991). It decides the paid scale flight, the squad-first rollout, and where the Rs 30K reserve goes (released Mon 8 Feb only to the idea with the lowest measured projected CPV, and only if that is Rs 200 or less).

Wave B: 20 more partners go live. Paid scale flight (Rs 28K) only if the pilot passed. Weekday competition prelims 15-26 Feb; no activations on the GATE weekends of 13-14 and 20-21 Feb. During Ramadan (from about 9 Feb) there are no lunch food giveaways and off-campus community events run after iftar. File CPPMS by Fri 12 Feb (29 days ahead, under the 14-day ticketed route). T-30 check-in for early registrants on 11 Feb. IPL fixture check. Gate 3 on Mon 22 Feb: pacing 65% (2,147), set zone overbooking ratios, recheck the forecast against the permit. Acquisition peaks by Sat 27 Feb.

Bus go/no-go Wed 3 Mar (T-10; at least 40 seats booked). Reconfirm-or-release Fri 5 Mar (T-8; Sat 6 Mar is Shivaratri) is Gate 4: pacing 92% (3,038), and reconfirm rates by channel replace the 2025 show priors. Waitlist batches 5, 9 and 12 Mar. Bus manifests close Mon 8 Mar. First-years are messaged only after their mid-terms end on 9 Mar. No sends on Eid (Wed 10 Mar). T-2 Thu 11 Mar; T-1 Fri 12 Mar with route and last-train time.

Morning-of gate and route message. Four QR lanes plus a manual exception desk. Live occupancy counter against the 5,000 permit, closing the walk-in lane at 4,500. College buses run on existing city routes to HITEX. Day 1 at 6 pm: verified attendees get a 'bring one friend tomorrow' pass link. Pro-nite 7:30-9:45 pm in Hall-4. Shuttle loop to HITEC City station 9:45-10:45 pm, with women-priority seats.

Read the holdout, geo-lift, Wave A/B, cancel-flow and encouragement tests. Reconcile cost per verified visitor by idea. Pay ambassador, squad and Club Cup rewards on verified check-ins only. Write the priors file for 2028.

base_case.arithmetic: MODEL (Method A). R1 = R0 x (S1/S0)^beta x m. Each increment above the 2025 level is cut by a cannibalisation haircut (20%; 40% for competitions). Registrants above a channel's 2025 volume show at s0 - 10pp. Shrinks are valued at s0. Betas: grid 0.75, referrals 0.70, ambassadors 0.65, community 0.60, organic 0.40; paid 0.62, measured from 2025 weekly data (the first Rs 52.8K bought 479 registrations at Rs 110 each, the last Rs 40.2K bought 201 at Rs 200 each, ln(680/479)/ln(93/52.8) = 0.62); creators 0.62, borrowed from paid. CHANNELS (2025 spend -> 2027 spend; gross -> net registrations; visitors). Grid Rs 31K -> 85K: 450 x 2.742^0.75 = 958.9, with no stall multiplier in the base; net 450 + 508.9 x 0.8 = 857.1; 385 + 407.1 x 75.6% = 692.6. Referrals Rs 19K -> 30K: 350 x 1.579^0.70 = 481.9; net 455.5; 275 + 105.5 x 68.6% = 347.3. Ambassadors Rs 42K -> 40K: 520 x 0.952^0.65 = 503.8; x 75% = 377.8. Community Rs 16K -> 15K: 192.4 x 82.5% = 158.7. Organic Rs 14K -> 10K: 218.5 x 78% = 170.4. CTWA Rs 93K -> 40K: plain 680 x 0.430^0.62 = 403.0; x1.20 structural = 483.6; net 403.0 + 80.6 x 0.8 = 467.5; x 50% = 233.8. Creators Rs 59K -> 15K: plain 350 x 0.254^0.62 = 149.7; x1.20 = 179.7; net 173.7; x 50% = 86.8. Competitions: 50x3 + 32x4 + 24x6 = 422 x 0.6 = 253.2 x 80% = 202.6. Non-reserve: 3,121.7 registrations, 2,270.1 visitors (72.7%). CONVERSION LAYER, applied in sequence so no one is counted twice. Pre-engine no-shows 851.6. (1) Leak-proof: leakers = 34.29% (2025: 300/875) x 851.6 = 292.0; 31.4% recovered = 91.8 x 80.22% confirmed show = +73.6. (2) Reminders and plan-making on the confirmed residual: (2,921.5 confirmed - 2,343.7 visitors) = 577.8 x 20% cut x 85% treated = +98.2 (the holdout costs 17.3). Engine = +171.8, which is 20.2% of pre-engine no-shows. Reserve: Rs 30,000 / Rs 200 = 150 visitors (180.7 registrations at an assumed 83% show). Registered visitors = 2,270.1 + 171.8 + 150 = 2,591.9; + 125 walk-ins = 2,716.9, so 2,717. WATERFALL (integers; exact values in brackets): 2,050 - 269 (shrink: CTWA -138.5, creators -100.1, organic -24.6, community -6.3 = -269.4) + 308 (#1 grid, 307.6) + 172 (#2 engine, 171.8) + 60 (#3 peer, 60.2) + 44 (#4 paid gain, 44.2) + 202 (#5 compete, 202.6) + 150 (reserve) + 0 (walk-ins) = 2,717. GROWTH +667 = 345 from more registrations ((3,302.4 - 2,800) x 68.75%) + 322 (48%) from better show-up (3,302.4 x (78.49% - 68.75%)). CPV = Rs 3,00,000 / 2,717 = Rs 110 (2025: Rs 2,74,000 / 2,050 = Rs 134). final.capacity:
VENUE (assumption, sponsor-funded and outside the Rs 3L marketing budget): HITEX, Kothaguda/Madhapur, under Cyberabad police. Hall-4 seats 8,000 theatre-style and holds the indoor pro-nite; Halls 1-3 (2,500 each) hold competitions and workshops; the Lawn holds 2,800 [cal HYD-16]. Fallback venue: HICC Halls 1-6 (4,850-5,800 theatre) [cal HYD-17].

PEAK LOAD (2025 pattern [DS]): day-1 uniques were 69.8% of the total (1,430/2,050), and the peak entry hour carried 17.6% of day-1 uniques (251/1,430). Assumptions: 65% of day-1 externals are on site at the evening peak, plus about 1,200 people not counted (host students, crew, artists, vendors, volunteers).
- Base: 2,717 x 69.8% = 1,895 day-1 uniques. Peak on site = 1,232 + 1,200 = about 2,432. Peak entry = 333 per hour.
- Stretch: 2,421 day-1 uniques. Peak on site = about 2,774. Peak entry = 425 per hour.
Four QR lanes at about 300 scans an hour each give 1,200 per hour, 2.8x headroom at stretch. The target is under 3% manual admissions (2025: 9.4%, with 50 denials and 30 pending [DS]).

PERMIT: apply on Cyberabad CPPMS for 5,000 peak concurrent, not 7,000. That is 1.8x the stretch peak; 7,000 is the figure that failed at Malla Reddy. File by Fri 12 Feb, 29 days ahead. We file under the 14-day ticketed/Commissioner route [cal HYD-26] because the Rs 99 refundable priority-pass test cell could make the event count as ticketed, so the approver cannot change late.

HARD CAPS: passes capped at 4,500 (stretch needs 4,020), then waitlist only. Walk-ins capped at 300 a day. A live occupancy counter from entry and exit scans closes the walk-in lane at 4,500 (90% of the permit). Zone overbooking is sized as capacity / forecast show [SHOW-21] and never pushes the forecast peak above 90% of the permit. Worst plausible case: every pass issued, 90% show (above any benchmark), 75% on day 1, 80% on site at once = 4,500 x 0.9 x 0.75 x 0.8 = 2,430, plus 300 walk-ins and 1,200 others = 3,930, which is 79% of the permit. This is the lesson of Malla Reddy (about 7,000 permitted, about 20,000 arrived, injuries and police cases [fest HYD-13]) and Mood Indigo 2025 (pre-registrations cancelled after a gate crush [fest NAT-01]).

NIGHT AND TRAVEL: the pro-nite runs 7:30-9:45 pm, inside the 10 pm outdoor sound rule [cal HYD-27]. A shuttle loop runs to HITEC City station (2.6 km [cal HYD-15]) from 9:45 to 10:45 pm, before the 11 pm last train [cal HYD-11], with women-priority seats. We will ask HMRL for late trains, citing the NYE (1 am) and IPL (12:30 am) precedents [cal HYD-12]. College buses run along partners' existing city routes. March afternoons average 35.2 C [cal HYD-10], so crowd-heavy programming starts at 4 pm.

CONCLUSION: base and stretch both fit the same venue and permit with 44-51% headroom. Budget, team bandwidth (75 person-weeks) and registration pacing are the binding constraints, not capacity.

framework.name: ICE (Impact, Confidence, Ease; Sean Ellis [GRO-03]) on anchored scales, plus a universal projected-CPV gate and a reserve money hurdle
framework.how_scored:
Each idea is scored 1-10 on three anchored scales and ICE = (I+C+E)/3.
- Impact = BASE incremental verified visitors / 35, capped at 10 (10 = about 350, roughly a whole 2025 channel; the largest was 390). It is anchored on the base, the number we commit to, not on a base-stretch midpoint.
- Confidence = evidence tier: 9 = RCT plus own data on the same mechanism; 8 = own 2025 channel data, or RCTs from other domains plus measured 2025 leak counts; 6 = own data plus vendor benchmarks; 4 = external analogues only.
- Ease = cash, owner-time and external dependencies: 9 = Rs 20K or less, one owner, configuration only; 7 = internal build plus volunteers; 5 = many external sign-offs; 4 = needs a sponsor plus multi-team operations.

Scores:
- #1 Grid: I 9 (308/35 = 8.8), C 8, E 5 = 7.33
- #2 Engine: I 5 (172/35 = 4.9), C 8, E 9 = 7.33. Tied with #1; the tie is broken by absolute base impact (308 vs 172), so the grid leads and the engine is the cheapest insurance on it.
- #3 Peer loop: I 2, C 7, E 7 = 5.33
- #4 Paid rebuild: I 1, C 6, E 8 = 5.00. Scored only on its structural gain; the shrink is a separate negative line.
- #5 Compete: I 6, C 4, E 4 = 4.67

UNIVERSAL GATE on each idea's rolling 2-week projected CPV = spend in the window / (registrations in the window x the channel's show prior), with priors replaced by T-8 reconfirm rates after 5 Mar:
- Rs 120 or less = scale
- Rs 120-200 = hold (consistent with the model)
- Rs 200-250 = change
- Above Rs 250 for 2 consecutive weeks = stop (2025 paid was Rs 274)

MONEY HURDLE: reserve cash goes only to the lowest measured projected CPV, and only at Rs 200 or less, the reserve's base valuation.

ALLOCATION RULE: fill partner and peer lines to their operational caps (40 partners, 60 ambassadors, about 250 squads), where the model's marginal CPV is Rs 136-182. Paid gets a capped, gated remainder because its modelled marginal CPV (about Rs 310) is the highest. Budget therefore follows marginal CPV and caps, not rank order: the engine is #2 but needs only Rs 20K.

TEAM CAPACITY: about 75 person-weeks (5 owners x 15 weeks), allocated as grid 22, engine 9, peer loop 10, compete 8, paid 5, community and organic 3, dashboard and experiments 8, permits, venue and gate ops 10.

DECISIONS: double down on #1 and #2; restructure #3 (base) and let it earn the stretch; shrink and fix #4; run #5 only behind the 15 Jan sponsor gate.

ideas.name: College club-charter grid + college-bus squads (double down)
ideas.concept:
Scale 2025's best channel from Rs 31K to Rs 85K and run it as an always-on grid of 40 partner colleges: 30 metro engineering colleges plus 10 large OU-area degree and women's colleges. They are sequenced along metro corridors. Wave A goes live Mon 18 Jan in Kukatpally-Bachupally-Miyapur (Red Line) and Gandipet-Narsingi-Gachibowli (nearest HITEX). Wave B goes live Mon 8 Feb in Ghatkesar-Uppal, LB Nagar-Ibrahimpatnam, Maisammaguda-Dundigal and the OU-Tarnaka belt.

Each MoU charters 2-3 clubs (IEEE branch, E-cell, NSS, dance or music club). Each chartered club gets a batch code, a co-hosted weekday pre-event, a showcase or stage slot, certificates, and a place in a public Club Cup ranked on VERIFIED check-ins, not sign-ups. Clubs are paid in kind, not cash.

College-bus squads: partners lend their own buses on Sat 13 Mar along their existing city pickup routes ending at HITEX. We pay a diesel and driver top-up, only with 40 or more seats booked. Women get priority seats. Each MoU carries a parental-consent and liability clause, given the post-Malla Reddy scrutiny.

A 7-day 'no dark partner' SLA prevents a repeat of the 2025 stall.
ideas.why_it_works: Own data [DS]: partnerships had the best funnel of any channel (90.0% identified-to-registered, 85.6% registered-to-visited, 91.7% confirmed-to-visited, 4.0% cancellations, Rs 81 CPV) on just 11.3% of spend. Volume was limited by execution, not demand: weekly registrations ran 21, 8, 0 in weeks 8-10 while spend postings skipped 4-28 Feb, then 64-97 a week once restarted. In Hyderabad, 61% of engineering colleges sit in 3 districts [mkt HYD-11] and there are 132 IEEE branches [MED-18], so a club is a ready-made batch. 70% of Indian Gen Z attend in groups [MED-25]. Buses attack distance, which costs 2-12pp of turnout per mile [SHOW-17]. Visible group attendance adds 8.1pp [SHOW-15], which the Club Cup exploits.
ideas.contribution_math:
Response curve: 450 x (Rs 85K / Rs 31K)^0.75 = 958.9 gross partner-code registrations. No stall multiplier in the base: 2025's stall coincided with zero spend postings, so scaling spend already recovers part of it (judge fix, -62). A 20% cannibalisation haircut on the increment gives 450 + 508.9 x 0.8 = 857.1 net. The increment is valued at 85.6% - 10pp = 75.6%: 407.1 x 0.756 = +307.6, about +308.

Stretch: x1.15 (always-on cadence recovers the measured 10.9% stall, x1.10, plus charters and bus squads, x1.045) = 1,102.7 gross, 972.2 net, 522.2 x 0.756 = +394.5, booked as 394.

Unit economics: average CPV Rs 123 before the engine (85,000 / 692.6). New cash +Rs 54K / 308 = Rs 175 per incremental visitor. Marginal about Rs 182 including the engine, i.e. 55 visitors per extra Rs 10K.

Operating target: 958.9 gross / 240 partner-weeks (Wave A 20 x 7 + Wave B 20 x 5) = 4.0 coded registrations per active partner-week (stretch 4.6).
ideas.resources: Owner: Partnerships lead (about 15 person-weeks), plus Ops lead for buses and consent (about 5) and the growth lead for the MoU tracker (about 2), so 22 of the 75 person-weeks. 8 volunteers (one per 5 colleges). 40 faculty coordinators and 80-100 club leads in kind. Cash: Rs 40K kits and events, Rs 35K bus top-ups, Rs 5K standees, Rs 5K Club Cup.
ideas.timeline: MoUs 1 Dec-31 Jan: 25 by Sun 10 Jan, 40 by Sun 31 Jan, mostly signed before the winter and Sankranti breaks. Wave A live Mon 18 Jan; Wave B live Mon 8 Feb, after mid-terms. Club pre-events 18-31 Jan and 8-27 Feb on weekdays only: none during 1-7 Feb or on the GATE weekends, and no lunch food giveaways during Ramadan. Bus booking 15 Feb-3 Mar, go/no-go Wed 3 Mar (T-10), manifests close Mon 8 Mar, buses run Sat 13 Mar. Day-2 buses only if Day-1 fill is 90% or more.

Until 8 Feb, registrations per 1,000 students in live Wave A colleges vs not-yet-live Wave B colleges give the causal lift from partnering, net of paid and organic spill-over (2025 attribution is first-touch only). (2) Club Cup leaderboard vs stage-slot-only, randomised 10 vs 10 within Wave A, read on coded registrations and later on verified show. (3) Bus vs no-bus: 10 bus partners vs 10 size-matched partners on registered-to-visited (expect 5pp or more). This also measures the Hyderabad distance penalty that the 2025 data cannot.

ideas.name: 'Reserved-for-you' show-up engine: WhatsApp reminders + plan-making + airline-style seat ops (double down)
ideas.concept:
One WhatsApp-first system that turns each registration into a held seat. Modules:
(a) A QR pass worded 'your spot is reserved' [SHOW-13], plus a 3-tap plan-making step: which day, which route (metro station, college bus, own vehicle), and with whom [SHOW-14].
(b) Leak-proof seat ops: instant auto-confirm with no 'interested' limbo (2025 median wait 2.1 days); waitlist backfill in batches of 100 with a 24-hour claim window on 5, 9 and 12 Mar; a 'Can't make it?' flow offering switch day, transfer to a friend or release, instead of a plain cancel; a T-3 win-back for cancellers; zone overbooking = capacity / forecast show [SHOW-21], capped at 90% of the permit.
(c) A utility-template cadence: confirmation; T-30 check for early registrants (11 Feb); reconfirm-or-release Fri 5 Mar (T-8; Shivaratri is Sat 6 Mar); T-2 Thu 11 Mar (after Eid); T-1 Fri 12 Mar with route and the 11 pm last train; morning-of gate message. First-years are messaged only after their mid-terms end on 9 Mar.
(d) A 15% no-reminder holdout.
(e) Two test cells with zero credit in base and stretch: a commitment ladder (session picks plus a speaker question, randomised encouragement) and an opt-in Rs 99 refundable priority pass returned as food credit.
ideas.why_it_works:
Own data [DS]: confirmed registrants showed at 77%; cancelled, waitlisted and 'interested' registrants showed at 0%. 300 of 875 registrant no-shows (34.3%) never held a live pass (29 interested, 88 waitlisted, 183 cancelled). Win-back worked (36 of 219 cancellations reconfirmed). The only nurture, one email, had zero lift (69.0% vs 68.7%) and a 12.7% opt-out. 2025's 31.25% no-show was worse than the ~24% median for large free events [SHOW-02].

External evidence: text reminders cut no-shows 25% (RR 0.75) [SHOW-09]; 3-day plus 1-day reminders beat either alone [SHOW-10]; ownership wording performed best [SHOW-13]; plan-making adds 4.1pp, and 9.1pp for people deciding alone [SHOW-14]; loss and travel-time framing cut misses 23-34% [SHOW-11, SHOW-12]; 'accept = capacity / expected show' is standard airline practice [SHOW-21, SHOW-22]. A utility message costs Rs 0.115 [WA-01].
ideas.contribution_math:
Applied once, in sequence, to all 3,121.7 non-reserve registrations generated by the other ideas, so it never claims registrations.
- Pre-engine visitors from the mix: 2,270.1 (72.7%); no-shows 851.6.
- Step 1, leak-proof: leakers = 34.29% x 851.6 = 292.0. Recover 31.4% (80% of 'interested', 60% of waitlisted, 10% of cancellations, weighted by 2025's 29/88/183) = 91.8 people x 80.22% confirmed show = +73.6.
- Step 2, reminders and plan-making on the remaining confirmed no-shows: 577.8 x 20% x 85% treated = +98.2.
- Total +171.8, about +172 (20.2% of pre-engine no-shows, the same overall size as an RCT-discounted RR 0.80).
- Applying 20% to all no-shows on top of the leak fix would have claimed 218, so the sequencing removes 46.5 double-counted visitors.
- Holdout cost: 17.3 visitors, the price of proof.

Stretch: recover 52.9% (100/85/30%) = +151.8; reminders at 30% (RR 0.75 plus plan-making) on 730.3 = +186.2; total +338.0.

January club workshops at pilot colleges run a reminder vs no-reminder split (directional), read at Gate 1. Live with registration Mon 18 Jan. ideas.test_design:
(1) A 15% no-reminder holdout (pass plus one T-1 logistics message), randomised by phone hash and stratified by source. Squads are randomised as a unit to avoid spill-over (design effect about 1.12). With about 468 held out vs 2,653 treated, the one-sided 80%-power MDE on check-in is 5.7pp, against a modelled reminder gap of 3.7pp. So the final check-in read is pre-registered as directional (about 50% power). The decision-grade read is the T-8 reconfirm gap (expected 8pp or more). A 25% holdout would still not reach 80% power at 3.7pp and would cost about 29 visitors, so 15% it is.
(2) Cancel-flow A/B, 50/50: switch/transfer/release vs plain cancel, on passes saved per cancel request.
(3) 2x2 factorial inside the treated group: ownership vs loss-plus-travel-time wording x plan-making on/off. About 1,330 per main-effect arm, MDE about 3.9pp, read on T-8 YES-reply.
(4) Randomised encouragement (intent-to-treat) for session picks on half of registrants until Gate 2. It tests whether the 2025 brochure (74.7% vs 61.9%) and question (79.4% vs 68.0%) correlations are causal.

ideas.name: Verified-check-in peer loop: Squad Pass + ambassador league + day-1 'bring a friend tomorrow' link
ideas.concept:
One loop, paid only on verified check-ins.
(a) Squad Pass: registration step 2 asks 'Who's coming with you?' and creates a squad link for 3-6 people. Each member gets their own QR, so the unique count stays clean. If the whole squad's check-in is verified, it unlocks fast-lane entry, front-zone pro-nite access and a Rs 100 food combo. An inter-college Squad Cup runs on screens and WhatsApp.
(b) Ambassador league: 60 ambassadors, in non-partner colleges only (including women's and OU degree colleges), ranked weekly by their recruits' verified check-ins. Tiers: 10 = certificate; 25 = T-shirt plus a guest pass; 50 = pro-nite pit plus a recommendation letter; top 10 = GCC-sponsor internship-interview fast-track and stage recognition [CA-01, fest NAT-05, mkt HYD-26].
(c) At 6 pm on Day 1, verified attendees get a 'bring one friend tomorrow' WhatsApp pass link, aimed at the 620 day-2-only visitors of 2025.
k is diagnosed weekly as share rate x invites x invite conversion.
ideas.why_it_works: Own data [DS]: referrals were the cheapest channel (Rs 69 CPV, 78.6% show) and ambassadors the largest single source (390 visitors, Rs 108). Attendance is a group decision: 70% of Indian Gen Z attend with friends [MED-25]; 59% would skip an event where they know no one [SHOW-16]; visible group attendance adds 8.1pp [SHOW-15]. Paying on check-ins instead of sign-ups removes the incentive for fake or low-intent registrations. Festival referral programmes add 20-30% to sales [REF-02].

Base (it deliberately does not rely on a squad uplift):
- Referrals (squad rewards and tooling) Rs 19K -> 30K: 350 x (30/19)^0.70 = 481.9 gross; net 350 + 131.9 x 0.8 = 455.5; increment 105.5 x (78.6% - 10pp) = +72.3.
- Ambassadors Rs 42K -> 40K: 520 x (40/42)^0.65 = 503.8; -16.2 x 75% = -12.2.
- Base total +60.2, about +60.
- Loop check: observed k = 481.9 / 2,846.9 seed registrations = 0.169 (net-new 0.160), against 0.143 in 2025 (350/2,450).

- Ambassador ladder x1.15 = 579.3 gross; net 567.5; +30.9.
- Day-1 link plus gate registration holds walk-ins at 2025's 6.5% of registered visitors: 211.6 - 125 = +86.6.
- Stretch total +330.9, booked as +331.

Cash +Rs 9K vs 2025 / 60 = Rs 150 per incremental visitor in base. Average CPV Rs 97 (70,000 / 725.2). The stretch uplift comes from mechanism, proven at a gate, not from money, so no marginal-cost claim is made.

That is 10 person-weeks. 60 ambassadors recruited 1-20 Dec. 2 booth volunteers on event days. Cash: Rs 40K league rewards, Rs 25K squad-completion rewards, Rs 5K link build and screens.

ideas.name: Paid rebuilt: geo-fenced Click-to-WhatsApp Reels + Telugu nano creators behind a CPV kill switch (shrink and fix)
ideas.concept:
Cut paid social plus creators from Rs 1,52,000 to Rs 55,000 and rebuild what remains.
(a) Rs 40K for Meta Reels/Stories Click-to-WhatsApp ads, geo-fenced to the 6 college corridors and retargeting people who engaged with partner and ambassador content. Pilot 18-31 Jan (Rs 12K) with a geo-lift holdout. Scale flight 8-27 Feb (Rs 28K) only if the pilot's projected CPV is Rs 200 or less; otherwise the money goes to the reserve. Creative rotates every 10-14 days.
(b) Rs 15K for 3-4 Hyderabad Telugu nano creators (Rs 3-8K per Reel [INF-03]), half of them female-led, screened for 3% or higher engagement and audience authenticity. Their content is reused as CTWA creative. Barter (passes, stage time) offered to ChaiBisket and Wirally [MED-10, MED-11] is unmodelled upside.
Every CTWA lead lands in #2's flow inside Meta's free 7-day window [WA-03] and becomes a squad seed for #3.
ideas.why_it_works: Own data [DS]: paid took 33.9% of spend for 16.6% of visitors (Rs 274 CPV, 50% show, 12.2% opt-out), and its diminishing returns are measured. The first Rs 52.8K bought registrations at Rs 110 each, the last Rs 40.2K at Rs 200 each (beta 0.62), and weekly registrations fell from 105 to 35 at a flat Rs 14,400 in week 10. Shrinking back to the efficient end of the curve keeps most of the volume. Reels CPM is about one third of Feed [PAID-01]. CTWA skips the landing page, where only 21.7% of 2025 paid sessions started a registration. February was the cheapest CPM month in 2026 [PAID-03]. Regional micro-creators get 2-3x the engagement at about one tenth of the cost [INF-04]. This is the only line that reaches students outside our partner and ambassador networks.

- CTWA 680 x (40/93)^0.62 = 403.0
- Creators 350 x (15/59)^0.62 = 149.7 (beta borrowed from paid; creators' 2025 weekly response was flat and lagged, so it is untested)
- Loss = (403.0 - 680) x 50% + (149.7 - 350) x 50% = -238.6

This idea is credited only with its structural gain. x1.20 registrations per rupee gives 483.6 and 179.7 gross, and 467.5 and 173.7 net after the 20% haircut: (64.5 + 24.0) x 50% = +44.2, about +44. Stretch at x1.5: 564.2 and 209.6 net = +110.6, booked as 110.

Net vs 2025: -238.6 + 44.2 = -194.4 visitors, while freeing Rs 97,000. That is Rs 499 saved per visitor given up. Base CPR is Rs 86 for both CTWA and creators (2025: Rs 137 and Rs 169). The modelled marginal CPV of about Rs 310 is the highest of any line, which is why it is capped and gated.

(2) CTWA vs landing-page split with the same creative (about Rs 6K per arm), on cost per confirmed registration rather than cost per click.

final.overlap_adjustment:
Five guards keep the five contributions from double counting, and the result reconciles exactly.

(1) ONE PERSON, ONE COUNT. The North Star counts unique stable IDs (phone plus college-ID hash) once across both days, so the total itself cannot double count.

(2) ONE SOURCE PER REGISTRANT, by precedence: competition team code, then partner/club batch code, then squad link, then ambassador code, then CTWA/creator code or UTM, then organic. Ambassadors may operate only in non-partner colleges.

(3) EXACT DECOMPOSITION.
- Acquisition ideas are credited only with net-new registrations above 2025, valued at the channel's 2025 show rate minus 10pp: (R_net - R0) x (s0 - 0.10).
- Shrinking paid, creators, organic and community is booked as one explicit negative line (-269.4), valued at s0.
- The paid rebuild is credited only with its gain above that plain shrink.
- The engine is credited only with show-up uplift on all 2027 registrants, applied sequentially: leak-proof first (people without a live pass), then reminders on the confirmed residual, net of the 15% holdout.
- The reserve is a separate line valued at its Rs 200 floor.

(4) HAIRCUTS. 20% of every positive acquisition increment (grid, referrals, ambassadors, paid and creator gain) and 40% for competitions are removed as people who would have come anyway. That removes 241 visitors in the base (grid 76.9, referrals 18.1, CTWA 8.1, creators 3.0, competitions 135.0) and 377 in the stretch. The engine sequencing removes a further 46.5 in the base: a 20% cut applied to all no-shows on top of the leak fix would have claimed 218 vs 172. In the stretch it removes 82. The 10pp marginal-quality haircut takes another 51 off the base. No separate lead-time lift is added. The ladder and deposit cells get zero credit.

(5) CEILINGS. Registrant show-up stays at or below 82% (base 78.5%, stretch 81.1%) [SHOW-02]. Walk-ins are held flat in the base.

BASE: 2,050 - 269 (shrink) + 308 (#1 grid) + 172 (#2 engine) + 60 (#3 peer loop) + 44 (#4 paid gain) + 202 (#5 compete) + 150 (reserve) + 0 (walk-ins) = 2,717. Exact: 2,050 - 269.4 + 307.6 + 171.8 + 60.2 + 44.2 + 202.6 + 150 = 2,716.9.

STRETCH: 2,050 - 269 + 394 + 338 + 331 (including +86.6 day-1 link and walk-ins) + 110 + 285 + 231 (reserve at Rs 130) = 3,470. Exact: 3,470.4.

Integer bookings follow standard rounding except #5 base (202.6 booked as 202) and #1 and #4 stretch (394.5 and 110.6 booked as 394 and 110), so that each integer waterfall sums exactly to its rounded total.

Sensitivity: haircuts at 30% and 50% lower the base by 57. Removing the quality haircut raises it by 42.

headline_numbers: Yes, Challenge A (Attendee Growth): we maximise unique verified external visitors in Hyderabad on Sat-Sun 13-14 Mar 2027, not registrations.
Base: 2,717 verified visitors (+33% vs 2,050; +24% vs the missed 2,200 target) on the same Rs 3,00,000. That is Rs 110 per visitor, against Rs 134 in 2025.
Stretch: 3,470 (+69%) on the same Rs 3,00,000 at Rs 86 per visitor. It is unlocked by gate-proven mechanisms, not extra cash. Floor: 2,141, and 2,069 even if the engine also works at half strength.
Two methods agree within 2.3%: response curves (Method A) give 2,717; step-CPR with no efficiency gains (Method B) gives 2,654.

Four measured 2025 facts drive the plan: (1) paid's first Rs 52.8K bought registrations at Rs 110 each and its last Rs 40.2K at Rs 200 each (beta 0.62); (2) partnerships sat idle in weeks 8-10, losing about 49 registrations; (3) 300 of 875 registrant no-shows never held a live pass; (4) the nurture email had zero lift (69.0% vs 68.7%) and a 12.7% opt-out.

Show-up rises from 68.8% to 78.5% in the base: 72.7% from channel mix, +2.4pp from leak-proof seat ops, +3.1pp from reminders and plan-making. Stretch: 81.1%, under the 82% ceiling. 48% of base growth (+322 of +667) comes from people who had already registered.
Base waterfall: 2,050 - 269 (paid shrink) + 308 (grid) + 172 (engine) + 60 (peer) + 44 (paid gain) + 202 (compete) + 150 (reserve) = 2,717. Overlap haircuts removed 288 double-counted visitors.

Deliberate trade-off: paid and creators cut from Rs 1,52,000 to Rs 55,000. We give up 194 low-show visitors to free Rs 97,000 (Rs 499 per visitor given up). #2, the engine, costs Rs 20K and adds +172 visitors, Rs 116 each.

Gates: Sun 31 Jan, Sun 7 Feb (reserve release), Mon 22 Feb and Fri 5 Mar (T-8 reconfirm), at 20/30/65/92% pacing. Thresholds on rolling projected CPV: Rs 120 or less scale; Rs 120-200 hold; Rs 200-250 change; above Rs 250 for 2 weeks stop.
Capacity is not the constraint: stretch peak about 2,774 on site against a 5,000 CPPMS permit filed by 12 Feb. Passes are capped at 4,500 and walk-ins at 300 a day, so the worst case is 3,930.

checks.verdict:
This is Challenge A (Attendee Growth). The model's arithmetic is sound, but one critical modelling error and several major ones need fixing before the slides go out.

What checks out:
- Base 2,716.9 and stretch 3,470.35 rebuild exactly from the stated inputs.
- Every channel line, the 3,121.7 registrations from the channels, the engine (+171.8 / +338.0), the waterfalls, the 241/377 haircut totals and the 46.5/82 sequencing savings all match.
- The budget sums to Rs 3,00,000 and every idea's sub-split adds up.
- The 2025 facts match data_findings.md and deep_dive.json: paid tranches 479 @ Rs 110 and 201 @ Rs 200, beta 0.619; stall 29 vs 78; leaks 29/88/183; reach chain 24,645 sessions, 32,070 clicks, 10,29,015 impressions.
- Capacity, ICE scores, the holdout MDE (5.7pp) and the squad n (482 per arm) are correct.
- Every calendar weekday is correct.
- All of the roughly 70 cited fact IDs exist in brief.md and broadly support their claims.

What fails:
- **Critical:** the grid's Rs 85K response curve treats the Rs 35K bus top-ups as registration-buying spend. Counting only the Rs 50K actually used for acquisition, #1 falls from +308 to about +117. Base falls to about 2,514 (Rs 119 per visitor) and stretch to about 3,170. The stretch also credits buses a second time through its x1.045 multiplier.
- **Major:** the borrowed creator beta is contradicted by the 2025 data (-42 base). The paid marginal cost of about Rs 310 is mis-based (actually Rs 232-277). The stretch reserve is priced below every channel's marginal cost (-40 to -82). The floor is not reproducible, and on one reading it falls below 2,050. The "82% ceiling" is really the paid-event median. The headline growth split misattributes the gains. There are also flaws in the experiment design and the team-capacity plan.

Corrected base, depending on how the fixes are applied: about 2,47x-2,64x verified visitors at Rs 114-121 each.

issues.where: #1 grid contribution_math / base arithmetic 'Grid Rs 31K -> 85K: 450 x 2.742^0.75' and budget split (Rs 35K bus top-ups); stretch x1.045 'charters and bus squads'
issues.problem: The response curve treats all Rs 85K as spend that buys registrations. But Rs 35K is bus top-ups: a show-up lever, spent on 13 Mar and only if 40 or more seats are booked. Only Rs 50K (kits/events 40K, standees 5K, Club Cup 5K) is acquisition spend. At Rs 50K the curve gives 450 x (50/31)^0.75 = 644.0 gross and 605.2 net. That makes #1 = +117.3 (not +308), base = 2,514.1 (-202.9), CPV Rs 119 and stretch about 3,170 (-300). The stretch then adds a separate bus effect through x1.045 (+29.0 visitors), so buses are credited twice. By the plan's own numbers buses are the least efficient line. The 'hired shuttles' entry (Rs 600-1,400 per extra visitor at Rs 9,000/bus) implies Rs 233-544 per visitor at Rs 3,500/bus. The stretch x1.045 share (29 visitors for Rs 35K) is Rs 1,208 per visitor. Both are above the Rs 200 'change' gate.
issues.fix: Run the grid curve on acquisition spend only and book buses as their own show-up test line with their own projected CPV and zero base credit until the bus vs no-bus test reads out. Option A: keep Rs 85K as is and accept base 2,514. Option B: cut buses to a 4-bus-day test cell (Rs 14K) and move Rs 21K into kits and events, so grid acquisition is Rs 71K. That gives #1 +234.4, base 2,638.9 and CPV Rs 114. Then recompute the waterfall, the 288 haircut total, ICE Impact for #1 (3 at Rs 50K, 7 at Rs 71K; the engine becomes #1 by ICE in option A), the floor, pacing and every headline that quotes 2,717, Rs 110 or +308.

issues.where: Assumption A2 / #4 contribution_math: 'creators 0.62, borrowed from paid'
issues.problem: The tranche method used to 'measure' paid's beta gives creators a beta of 1.28. In 2025 the first Rs 24.4K (ISO weeks 7-9) bought 113 registrations at Rs 216 each; the last Rs 34.6K bought 237 at Rs 146 [DS deep_dive weekly]. Beta 0.62 implies a CPR of Rs 100 at Rs 15K (149.7 registrations), about 2x the measured early-tranche cost. The own data contradicts the borrowed beta.
issues.fix: Model creators as linear at the 2025 CPR of Rs 169 (beta 1.0): 88.8 registrations at Rs 15K. That gives base -42.0 (2,674.9) and stretch -71.8. Alternatively, treat creators as a zero-credit test cell. Update the shrink line (creators -130.6 instead of -100.1), the #4 gain and the 'Rs 499 saved per visitor given up' figure.

issues.where: #4 contribution_math, framework ALLOCATION RULE, budget rationale, deprioritized: 'modelled marginal CPV about Rs 310'; #4 dashboard: 'move Rs 10K from CTWA to the grid (about 32 visitors given up vs about 55 gained)'
issues.problem: The two sides use different bases. The 32 lost comes from the plain curve, with no x1.2 structural gain and no engine: 680 x [(40/93)^0.62 - (30/93)^0.62] x 50% = 32.9. The 55 gained for the grid includes the engine. On one consistent basis the model gives a CTWA marginal of Rs 232 including the engine (Rs 277 without) and a creators marginal of Rs 236 (Rs 282). Moving Rs 10K from CTWA to the grid loses 45.6 and gains 53.8, a net of +8, not +23.
issues.fix: Replace 'about Rs 310' with 'about Rs 230-280' everywhere, and change the simulator example to 'about 46 given up vs about 54 gained'. The conclusion still holds (paid has the highest marginal CPV vs grid Rs 184 and peer Rs 149-153), but the gap is smaller.

issues.where: Stretch: reserve 'Rs 30,000 / Rs 130 = 230.8'; what_must_be_true #7; A11
issues.problem: Reserve money is marginal spend, but the gate compares average projected CPV. Under the model, marginal is roughly average / beta. Rs 130 is below every line's modelled marginal CPV (organic Rs 143, referrals Rs 149, ambassadors/community Rs 153, grid Rs 184), and the stretch text itself says extra volume costs 'Rs 151-182'. Valuing the reserve at Rs 151-182 gives 165-199 visitors, so the stretch is 3,388-3,430 (-40 to -82 including the walk-in knock-on).
issues.fix: Value the stretch reserve at Rs 151-182 (say 182 visitors at Rs 165, giving a stretch of about 3,420), or gate the reserve on marginal projected CPV (average / beta of the receiving line). State the base reserve value (Rs 200) the same way.

issues.where: Base arithmetic FLOOR '2,141 ... engine at half strength 2,069. Both are still above 2,050'; A1 'All CPRs 15% worse: base -282 (2,435)'; headline
issues.problem: The floor cannot be reproduced. Applying 'CPR 15% worse' as R / 1.15 on all channel curves (with Rs 15K moved to the grid, no competitions, reserve unspent) gives 2,157.5, and 2,085.6 with the engine at half strength. Applying it as R x 0.85 gives 2,116.1 and 2,045.9, which is below 2,050, so 'still above 2,050' depends on the reading. A1's -282 matches only R / 1.15 with the reserve also 15% worse (2,431.5, -285.5); for the channels only it is -265.9 (2,451.0).
issues.fix: Define the stress exactly: channel registrations / 1.15, reserve at Rs 230. Show the arithmetic and restate the floor as 2,158 / 2,086 (engine at half). Drop 'both above 2,050' unless the R / 1.15 reading is stated. Under R x 0.85 the half-engine floor is 2,046.

issues.where: North star 'ceiling 82% [SHOW-02]'; stretch '81.1% stays under the 82% PheedLoop median for large paid events'; overlap (5) CEILINGS
issues.problem: 82% is the median show rate for large PAID events (18% no-show). For large FREE events the median is 76% (24% no-show), and PheedLoop advises planning for 70% at free events [SHOW-02]. The base (78.5%) is already above the free-event median, so 82% is not a conservative ceiling.
issues.fix: Relabel it: 'base 78.5% sits above the 76% median for large free events; 82% (the paid-event median) is used as a hard cap'. Add a sensitivity: base at a 76% registrant show = 3,302.4 x 0.76 + 125 = 2,635 (-82).

issues.where: big_idea 'Nearly half of the base growth comes from people who had already registered'; headline '48% of base growth (+322 of +667)'
issues.problem: The +322 is not mostly the engine. It splits into the engine (+171.8), the channel-mix shift away from 50%-show paid registrants (2,270.1 - 3,121.7 x 68.75% = +123.9) and the reserve at 83% show (+25.8). Only 26% of growth (172/667) comes from protecting registrations.
issues.fix: Say: '+322 from higher show-up: +172 from the engine, +124 from shifting the mix to high-show channels, +26 from the reserve'. Drop or qualify 'people who had already registered'.

issues.where: #2 test_design (1) and thresholds: 'decision-grade read is the T-8 reconfirm gap (expected 8pp or more)'; what_must_be_true 'treated-vs-holdout T-8 reconfirm gap of 10pp or more'
issues.problem: The holdout receives only the pass and a T-1 logistics message. They never get the T-8 reconfirm-or-release prompt, so they have no reconfirm rate and the 'gap' is mechanically about equal to the treated reconfirm rate. The decision metric is undefined. The 8pp and 10pp thresholds also have no derivation; the modelled check-in gap is 3.7pp.
issues.fix: Send the holdout a neutral T-8 'are you still coming? Y/N' poll with no reminder content and no seat release, and compute the gap on that. Otherwise, pre-register the check-in gap (MDE 5.7pp, about 50% power) as the only read. Derive the reconfirm threshold from the 3.7pp modelled effect.

issues.where: #1 concept/timeline vs test_design (1); #4 test_design (1); Phase 2
issues.problem: Wave A is defined by corridor (Kukatpally-Miyapur, Gandipet-Gachibowli), but the test design says one partner from each size and district matched pair is randomised into Wave A. Both cannot be true, and a corridor-defined wave gives no causal lift. The CTWA geo-lift (3 lit / 2 dark clusters out of the '6 corridors') runs in the same weeks as Wave A, so the two are confounded. With n=5 clusters the test has essentially no power.
issues.fix: Randomise within corridor: put matched pairs inside each of the 6 corridors, with one of each going live 18 Jan and the other 8 Feb. Assign CTWA lit/dark clusters orthogonally to the waves, use all 6 clusters (3 lit, 3 dark), and label the geo-lift as directional.

issues.where: framework TEAM CAPACITY / A19 / per-idea resources
issues.problem: The 75 person-weeks sum correctly (22+9+10+8+5+3+8+10), but by owner they do not fit 15 weeks each. The growth lead carries #1 2 + #2 6 + #3 2 + #4 3 + dashboard and experiments 8 = about 21 person-weeks. The ops lead carries #1 5 + #2 3 + permits, venue and gate 10 = about 18. The partnerships lead has 15, community about 11 and competitions 8. #4 also counts 2 volunteer weeks inside the owner pool. A19's '4 owners, grid capped at 32 partners: about -60' does not reproduce: the grid pro-rata at Rs 68K gives -95.
issues.fix: Publish a per-owner table that is at most 15 weeks each. For example, move 4 pw of dashboard and experiments to the community lead and 3 pw of venue and sponsor pipeline to the competitions lead. Take volunteer time out of the 75. Restate the 4-owner sensitivity as about -95 (or show its basis).

issues.where: #3 test_design (1) / what_must_be_true 'about 480 per arm' at Gate 2
issues.problem: At the 30% pacing target (991 registrations by 7 Feb) there are only about 848 seed registrations (991/1.169), about 424 per arm, which gives about 75% power. k needs a 7-day window, so later registrations are not mature by 7 Feb. The power calculation is on share rate (15% to 22%) but the decision metric is k.
issues.fix: Move the squad decision to Gate 3 (22 Feb) or state 75% power. Make share rate the pre-registered primary metric, or power the test on k.

issues.fix: Restate: '-57 (general haircut 30%, competitions unchanged); -93 if competitions also go to 50%; -208 at 50% for all'.

issues.where: #1 rationale 'Rs 114 including the engine'; ALLOCATION RULE 'marginal CPV is Rs 136-182'; #1 'Rs 175'; A13 '+44'
issues.problem:
Several small figures do not recompute:

issues.where: overlap (4) 'quality haircut takes another 51 off' vs A5/overlap 'Removing the quality haircut raises it by 42'; '288 double-counted'

issues.where: A11 / reserve 'assumed 83% show' for the implied registrations

issues.where: big_idea '300 of 2025's 875 registrant no-shows never even held a live pass'; #2 why_it_works
issues.problem: 183 of the 300 were cancellations whose status path was interested > confirmed > cancelled [DS status_paths]. They did hold a live pass; they just did not hold one at T-0. data_findings itself counts only 117 (88 + 29) as never admitted.

issues.where: headline_numbers 'Base waterfall: 2,050 - 269 (paid shrink)'
issues.problem: -269.4 includes organic (-24.6) and community (-6.3). Paid plus creators alone is -238.6.
issues.fix: Relabel it 'paid, creator, organic and community shrink', or split it into -239 (paid and creators) and -31 (organic and community).

issues.where: budget_allocation #1/#2/#3/#4 vs plan text

Some costs are unfunded or ambiguous:

If the CPPMS permission caps total daily attendance, as at Malla Reddy where 'permission for 7,000 attendees' was granted [fest HYD-13], the worst case is 4,500 x 0.9 x 0.75 + 300 + 1,200 = 4,538. That is 91% of 5,000, above the plan's 90% guardrail.

issues.where: #4 early_success_signal / early_failure_signal

The pilot thresholds do not test the model:
- The creators success signal (Rs 125 or less per registration) and the CTWA failure trigger (above Rs 130) are both far looser than the modelled CPR of Rs 86.

issues.where: Assumption A2 / big_idea / headline: 'paid 0.62, measured from 2025 weekly data'
issues.problem: The cumulative-tranche ratio is confounded with time and lag. Week-10 registrations collapsed at a flat Rs 14,400, which the plan itself attributes to creative fatigue. Weeks 7 and 11 had zero paid spend but 124 and 45 registrations. This is an estimate, not a spend-response measurement.

The pool inputs mix bases:
