checks.verdict:
Yes, this is Challenge A (Attendee Growth). The plan's arithmetic holds up: the base waterfall reconciles exactly to 2,716.9 (stretch 3,470.4), every date in the timeline falls on the weekday stated (13 Mar 2027 is a Saturday, 5 Mar a Friday, 22 Feb a Monday, and so on), and the capacity numbers recompute. Feasibility and logic do not hold up yet. Three critical flaws break Slide 3 and the base:
(1) The 15% holdout never receives the T-8 message, so the "decision-grade" T-8 reconfirm gap the engine is gated on cannot be measured.
(2) "Reconfirm-or-release" would cancel live passes for people who don't reply, including first-years muted 3-9 Mar, even though capacity never binds (4,500 pass cap against a 5,000 permit; stretch peak about 2,774).
(3) Pacing needs 539-567 registrations a week in the base (1.5-1.6x 2025's peak week of 354) and 657-691 in the stretch (1.85-1.95x). That falls in a registration window about 4 weeks shorter than 2025's, with GATE weekends, Ramadan and first-year mid-terms inside it.

There are 17 major issues. The main ones:
- The growth lead carries 21 person-weeks in 15 weeks (140%) and the ops lead 18 (120%).
- The projected-cost-per-visitor gate can't be measured before the event for #2 and #3, and it uses no show-quality signal before 5 Mar.
- The reserve rule would send cash to #5 (Rs 74 on cash alone) or #3 (about Rs 0 before rewards are paid), and neither can absorb it.
- The sponsor-gated #5 (+202) is counted in the "realistic" base.
- The paid and creator curve is extrapolated below observed spend (+58 visitors that the evidence doesn't support).
- The rule to switch dates when IPL fixtures come out (mid-Feb) can't be executed after registration, permits and bus bookings are tied to 13-14 Mar.
- The Eid holidays (Wed-Thu) plus a second Saturday make a 5-day bridge break around the fest.
- There is no date for locking the venue.
- Buses cost Rs 583-875 per extra visitor, the same economics used to reject hired shuttles.
- The Wave A/B test, the paid geo-lift and the squad A/B can't be run as designed.
- Assuming the free Luma plan covers the integrations is unverified, and the copilot needs person-level data while claiming to send only non-personal data.
- The content cannot fit 3 slides.

After the fixes, a base that doesn't depend on a sponsor is about 2,550-2,620 (sponsor-gated work removed or probability-weighted, paid capped at measured cost per registration, waitlist leak fully recovered). Present 3,470 as a target unlocked at the gates, not a projection.

issues.where: #2 test_design (1), KPI 'T-8 reconfirm: treated >=75% and >=8pp above holdout', Gate 4 early_success_signal, A8
issues.problem: The holdout gets only the pass and one T-1 logistics message, so it never receives the Fri 5 Mar reconfirm-or-release prompt. A holdout reconfirm rate therefore cannot exist, and the 'decision-grade' T-8 gap and the Gate 4 test cannot be measured. The only read left is check-in, which the plan admits is about 50% power (MDE about 5.5-5.7pp against a modelled 3.7pp).
issues.fix: Send the T-8 prompt to 100% of registrants as a measurement tool; the holdout is never released. Redefine the holdout as 'no ownership wording, no plan-making, no T-30', so the treatment is everything before T-8 and the T-8 YES gap (about 468 vs 2,653) measures it. Test T-2, T-1 and morning-of with a second randomisation at T-8 (for example, 15% get the morning-of message only), read on check-in as directional. Rewrite the KPI, Gate 4 and A8 to match.

issues.where: #2 concept (b)/(c) 'reconfirm-or-release', waitlist batches 5/9/12 Mar, zone overbooking; action_on_change 'non-responders' seats go to the waitlist'; capacity HARD CAPS
issues.problem: General entry never binds: passes are capped at 4,500 against a 5,000 permit, and the stretch peak is about 2,774. Releasing the passes of non-responders, or of whole channels whose YES rate is under 60%, cancels people who would have come (2025 confirmed show was 77%, and WhatsApp reply rates are far below 100%). That subtracts directly from the North Star. First-years are muted until 9 Mar, so all of them would be non-responders on 5 Mar. The waitlist and overbooking modules add ops load with no capacity reason.
issues.fix: For general entry, make T-8 'reconfirm', not 'reconfirm-or-release': a missing reply never voids a QR. Release only in named capacity-limited sub-zones (pro-nite front zone, workshop halls, hackathon seats), and only after an explicit 'No' or two unanswered prompts. Remove the general waitlist (auto-confirm everyone under 4,500) and set waitlist-leak recovery to 100% (about +27 base visitors). Drop zone overbooking outside the named sub-zones and give the freed ops time (about 2 person-weeks) to gate operations.

issues.where: A18 pacing; timeline phases 1-5; Gate 1-4 pacing thresholds; Phase 1 'interest list opens 21 Dec'
issues.problem:
Registration opens 18 Jan (54 days out), against about 12 weeks of registration in 2025. Recomputed weekly needs:
- Base: 539 a week (8-22 Feb) and 567 a week (22 Feb-5 Mar), 1.52-1.60x 2025's peak week of 354.
- Stretch: 657-691 a week (1.85-1.95x).
Those weeks include two GATE weekends, Ramadan and first-year mid-terms. Gate 2 also expects 330 registrations in the 1-7 Feb exam week, when there are no pushes at all. The interest list holds leads for 4 weeks, but 2025's identified-to-registered lag was at most 14 days (median 7), so the data does not support converting stale leads at 80%. There is no interest-list target, and the spend-based response curves have no time dimension.
issues.fix: Open registration on Mon 4 Jan to the interest list and organic traffic; campus waves stay on 18 Jan and 8 Feb. Early-registrant drift is covered by [SHOW-03] (within one event, early and late registrants differ by 0.6pp) and by the T-30 check. Add Gate 0 on Sun 17 Jan: at least 1,000 interest-list opt-ins and at least 400 registrations. Re-derive pacing week by week from 2025's weekly shape, with 1-7 Feb capped at about 150. If any week still needs more than 1.3x 2025's peak (about 460), lower the base or move the stretch work earlier.

issues.where: framework TEAM CAPACITY; A19; resources of every idea; all test_design fields
issues.problem:
Summing the resources lines gives:
- Growth/analytics lead: 2 (MoU tracker) + 6 (engine) + 2 (squad model) + 3 (paid) + 8 (dashboard and experiments) = 21 person-weeks in 15 weeks (140%).
- Ops lead: 5 + 3 + 10 = 18 (120%).
- Competitions and sponsors lead: 8 (53%), while also carrying the venue, production, shuttle and prize sponsor pipeline, which no line accounts for.
The owners are students, and no hours-per-week basis is stated. About 16 experiments run at once, some with n = 2 clusters (ambassador pay-on-verified vs pay-on-registration) or 10 vs 10 colleges.
issues.fix:
Define an owner-week as about 25 hours. Rebalance so no owner exceeds 15 person-weeks:
- Paid (3) moves to the Community lead.
- The MoU tracker (2) moves to partnership volunteers.
- Sponsor pipeline and CPPMS paperwork (3) move from Ops to the Competitions and sponsors lead.
Cut to 5 pre-registered tests tied to decisions: the matched-pair Wave A/B, the squad A/B, the redesigned holdout, the cancel-flow A/B, and a college-level CTWA geo test. Move the ladder, the Rs 99 deposit, the 2x2 wording factorial, Club Cup vs stage-slot, the ambassador pay model, CTWA vs landing page and the day-1 link randomisation to an 'only if bandwidth allows at Gate 2' list.

issues.where: framework UNIVERSAL GATE and every idea's scale/change/stop thresholds; north_star input (3)
issues.problem:
Projected CPV = spend / (registrations x 2025 show prior), and the priors are replaced only by T-8 reconfirm rates on 5 Mar. That is after Gate 2 (reserve release), Gate 3 and the 27 Feb acquisition peak, so every gate before T-8 is really a cost-per-registration gate. It also can't be measured before the event for most ideas:
- #2 produces no registrations.
- #3 pays rewards 15-25 Mar, so its pre-event cash is about Rs 0 and it always reads 'scale'.
- #1's cash is lumpy (Rs 40K of kits up front, Rs 35K of buses on 13 Mar), so its rolling cash CPV swings between 'stop' and 'scale'.
The dashboard's 85.6% grid prior also conflicts with the model's 75.6% marginal value, which biases the gate toward 'scale'.
issues.fix:
(a) Compute CPV on accrual: spread kit costs over each partner's live weeks, accrue #3's reward liability as projected check-ins x reward rate, and book bus top-ups when a bus is confirmed.
(b) Replace the constant prior with an engagement-adjusted show score per registrant, available within 72 hours and calibrated on 2025 data: brochure download 74.7% vs 61.9%, question submitted 79.4% vs 68.0%, plus WhatsApp opt-in and plan-making completion (labelled assumptions). Report it by channel from Gate 1.
(c) Use the 11 Feb T-30 reply rate as the Gate 3 show signal.
(d) Gate #2 on its own instruments (opt-in, plan completion, save rate, redesigned T-8 gap), not CPV.
(e) Set the dashboard prior to the model's blended channel show (grid 692.6 / 857.1 = 80.8%).

issues.where: framework MONEY HURDLE; budget 'Performance reserve'; scale_threshold of #1, #3 and #4; A11; A15
issues.problem: The rule gives the Rs 30K to the idea with the lowest measured average projected CPV. On cash, #5 reads Rs 74 (prizes excluded) and #3 reads about Rs 0, and neither can absorb money: competition slots are fixed by halls and the sponsor, and squads and ambassadors are capped. An average CPV also understates the marginal cost of the next rupee (grid average Rs 123 vs marginal about Rs 196). The same Rs 30K is promised to Wave C partners (Rs 15-30K), a 6+ squad tier (Rs 10K), the paid scale flight (Rs 15K) and the shuttle backstop, while being valued at 150 visitors in the base and 231 in the stretch. Wave C partners would go live on 8 Feb with no signed MoUs. The partner cap is stated as both 40 and 48.
issues.fix: Rewrite the rule: 'At Gate 2 the reserve funds the HITEC City shuttle first if no sponsor has signed by Fri 5 Feb (it is part of the CPPMS traffic plan due 12 Feb). The rest goes to the eligible idea with the lowest measured MARGINAL projected CPV (change in accrued spend / change in projected visitors between Gate 1 and Gate 2) that has named room to absorb it: grid Wave C (8 standby MoUs pre-signed by 31 Jan) or the paid scale flight. #3 and #5 are ineligible.' Use one partner cap (48, including standbys). Value the reserve in the base only if the shuttle is sponsored.

issues.where: #1 concept (Wave A = two named corridors) vs #1 test_design (1); timeline '25 MoUs by 10 Jan, 40 by 31 Jan'; #4 geo-lift in the same corridors
issues.problem: Wave A is defined both by geography (Kukatpally-Miyapur and Gandipet-Gachibowli) and as 'one of each matched pair randomised', which is contradictory. Pairing all 40 partners needs all 40 signed before 18 Jan, but only 25 are due by then. The clean comparison window is 18-31 Jan only, because 1-7 Feb has no campus pushes. The CTWA lit and dark clusters run in the same corridors in the same weeks, which confounds the read.
issues.fix: Randomise within each corridor. Pair the partners signed by 10 Jan (about 24, i.e. 12 pairs); one of each pair goes live 18 Jan and the other 8 Feb. Late signers go live 8 Feb outside the experiment. Read registrations per 1,000 students from all sources at Gates 1 and 2. Balance CTWA lit and dark areas across Wave A and B partners, or exclude partner campuses from CTWA targeting until 8 Feb. Then drop the claim that Wave A is sequenced by corridor; alternatively keep the corridor sequencing and claim only a before/after difference-in-differences, not causal lift.

issues.where: #4 test_design (1); KPI 'Lit clusters >=15% above dark'; #4 scale/stop thresholds ('no geo-lift' = stop)
issues.problem: 3 lit vs 2 dark clusters over 2 weeks, on a Rs 12K pilot (about 140 registrations at Rs 86 each), cannot detect a 15% lift. With 5 units, both 'positive geo-lift' (scale) and 'no geo-lift' (stop) are noise, so the thresholds aren't measurable leading indicators.
issues.fix: Randomise at college level: geo-fence 2 km radii around about 40 non-partner metro engineering colleges, 20 lit and 20 dark, stratified by corridor and size, and read registrations per 1,000 seats. Pre-register that Gate 2 decides on cost per registration plus the engagement-adjusted show score. Treat the geo-lift as directional unless its 90% confidence interval excludes zero, and remove 'no geo-lift' as an automatic stop trigger.

issues.where: #3 test_design (1); scale_threshold 'squad-first k >=0.22 at Gate 2'; stretch what_must_be_true (k 0.22)
issues.problem: The 480-per-arm sample size is computed for share rate (15% to 22%), but the gate uses k 'within 7 days'. Registrations with a full 7-day window by Gate 2 are the 660 due by 31 Jan, about 330 per arm, and only if pacing hits plan. Splitting the first 30% of registrations 50/50 also caps season k at about 0.208, so the stretch's 0.22 can't be reached even if squad-first works.
issues.fix: Make 48-hour share rate the Gate 2 decision metric, with k as directional. Pre-commit: roll squad-first out to 100% if the share-rate gap is at least 5pp at p < 0.1 by Gate 2, otherwise extend the test to Gate 3. Restate the stretch requirement as post-rollout k of at least 0.23 (season about 0.22), or cut about 40 registrations from the stretch referral line.

issues.where: timeline 'Fest dates' (switch to 20-21 Mar if SRH plays at home); Phase 4 'IPL fixture check'
issues.problem: Fixtures arrive in mid-February, after registration (18 Jan), the MoUs, bus bookings and the CPPMS filing (12 Feb) are all tied to 13-14 Mar, so a switch then can't be executed. Uppal is under the Malkajgiri commissionerate [cal HYD-28], not Cyberabad, which weakens the police-bandwidth argument. The fallback weekend was not checked: Sun 21 Mar is Holika Dahan [cal HYD-05] and Inter exams run to 20 Mar.
issues.fix: Lock 13-14 Mar by 15 Dec and delete the switch rule. If SRH has a home match, mitigate instead: end the pro-nite by 9:30 pm, run the shuttle until 10:30 pm so the fest crowd clears the Blue Line before the match crowd, and ask HMRL to extend service, citing the IPL precedent [cal HYD-12]. If a fallback is still named, state its costs: day 2 must end by 6 pm for Holika Dahan, and it is hotter.

issues.where: city_rationale 'A clean date'; show-up model (A7; base 78.5%); T-2 on Thu 11 Mar
issues.problem: Eid falls on Wed 10 Mar, Thu 11 Mar is the 'Following Day of Ramazan' holiday [cal HYD-04], and Sat 13 Mar is a second Saturday. Taking Fri 12 off gives a 5-day break, so hostel and PG students from other districts may go home over the fest weekend; the model doesn't account for this. If 30% of registrants are hostellers and their show-up drops 10pp, that is about -100 visitors. Eid also depends on moon sighting, so it could land on Thu 11, the T-2 send day.
issues.fix: Add 'Will you be in Hyderabad on 13-14 Mar?' to plan-making and the T-8 prompt, and forecast show separately by answer. Weight targeting toward colleges with mostly day scholars. Ask each partner whether Fri 12 Mar is a working day. Add a sensitivity line (about -100 visitors). If Eid moves to Thu 11, merge T-2 into the Fri 12 T-1 message.

issues.where: Phase 5 and #2 timeline 'first-years messaged only after their mid-terms end on 9 Mar'; bus go/no-go Wed 3 Mar; reconfirm Fri 5 Mar; manifests close Mon 8 Mar
issues.problem: First-years (about 25% of P1) are muted from 3 to 9 Mar, which covers the bus go/no-go, the T-8 reconfirm and the manifest close. They can't book buses or reconfirm, and under release rules they would lose their passes. The registration form doesn't capture year of study, so the mute can't even be applied.
issues.fix: Add a 'year of study' field to registration. Send first-years their bus booking and reconfirm message on Tue 2 Mar, before their mid-terms. Exempt them from any release, hold a first-year bus-seat block open until Thu 11 Mar, and leave them out of the Gate 4 channel recalibration (or weight them separately).

issues.where: Phase 0 'The venue (HITEX) and production sponsor are an out-of-scope dependency'; capacity (fallback HICC); CPPMS filing by 12 Feb
issues.problem: There is no date for locking the venue. Yet registration opens 18 Jan with a location, buses run routes ending at HITEX, and the CPPMS filing on 12 Feb needs the venue and its NOCs. HITEX's mid-March availability is unchecked. The fallback, HICC, is in the same complex, so its availability is correlated with HITEX's. Hall-4 plus Halls 1-3 for 2 days will cost several times the cited Shilpakala Rs 2.43L per day, and that sponsor ask has no date.
issues.fix: Add a venue-and-date lock gate on Fri 18 Dec (sponsor-paid deposit, or the plan pivots). Name a fallback with a different owner, for example G.M.C. Balayogi Indoor Stadium [cal HYD-20], whose 3,500-5,000 capacity would bind the stretch, or a large partner campus. Put dated sponsor milestones on the timeline: venue 18 Dec, prize pool 12 Jan, shuttle 5 Feb.

issues.where: city_rationale 'after the Elan, Felicity and Pearl window (Jan-Feb)'; Phase 0
issues.problem:
The 'clean date' claim uses 2026 fest dates, but these fests move between years:
- Elan went from 21-23 Feb 2025 to 9-11 Jan 2026 [fest HYD-03, HYD-01].
- CBIT Shruthi ran 4-8 Mar 2025 and then moved to Feb [fest HYD-11].
- A BITS-H public show ran on 29 Mar [fest HYD-08].
The 40 partners' own 2027 fest dates aren't checked, and a partner holding its own fest near 13-14 Mar will neither promote ours nor send students.
issues.fix: By 15 Dec, collect 2027 fest dates for the 60 shortlisted colleges and the flagship campuses. Make 'no own fest within 7 days either side of 13-14 Mar' an MoU screening criterion. Show any known 2027 clashes on the slides.

issues.where: #1 budget (Rs 35K bus top-ups, 10 bus-days); deprioritised 'Hired shuttles'; stretch grid x1.045 ('charters and bus squads')
issues.problem: The base averages about 24 gross partner-code registrations per partner (958.9/40), so a single college rarely reaches the 40-seats-booked threshold. At 40 riders and a 10-15pp show lift, a Rs 3,500 bus-day costs Rs 583-875 per extra visitor. That is the same economics used to reject hired shuttles (Rs 600-1,400) and 5-7x the engine's Rs 116. Buses act on show rate, yet the stretch books them as a registration multiplier. Day-2 buses have no budget.
issues.fix: Allow buses shared by 2-3 neighbouring partners in a corridor so they reach 40 seats. Cut the line to a Rs 14K pilot (4 bus-days in the two densest corridors). Move Rs 5K to organic and community (see the marginal-CPV issue) and Rs 16K to the reserve. Justify the pilot on women's night-time access, not CPV. Model buses as a show-rate uplift for riders in the conversion layer, not as x1.045 on registrations.

issues.where: base_case waterfall (+202 from #5, +150 reserve); headline 'Base: 2,717'
issues.problem: The 'realistic' base counts #5 at full value (+202.6, or about 213 including engine uplift), although it exists only if an unsigned Rs 2-3L prize sponsor commits by 15 Jan (Confidence 4). The +150 reserve may instead go to the shuttle. Reviewers penalise unsecured upside booked as base.
issues.fix: Lead with a base that doesn't depend on a sponsor: 2,717 - 213 + 82 (Rs 15K moved to the grid) = about 2,586. Show +131 as a 'sponsor-unlocked' band between base and stretch. Alternatively, probability-weight #5 (for example, 50% gives about 2,650) and state the weight. Say explicitly that the reserve's +150 assumes the shuttle is sponsored.

issues.where: #4 contribution_math; base arithmetic for CTWA and creators; #4 why_it_works 'keeps most of the volume'
issues.problem:
The power curve is extrapolated below the observed spend range:
- Plain-shrink CTWA comes out at Rs 99 per registration before the x1.2 gain. That beats paid's best measured tranche (Rs 110) and its best week (Rs 131 in week 6).
- Creators borrow paid's beta even though their weekly response was flat and lagged, which gives Rs 100 per registration against a measured Rs 169.
Together this inflates the base by about 58 visitors (CTWA -23, creators -35).
issues.fix: Cap the shrink at measured costs: paid at Rs 110 per registration, creators linear at Rs 169 (Method B already does this). The shrink line becomes about -320, the #4 gain about +36, and the base about 2,655 (Method B gives 2,654). Replace 'keeps most of the volume' with 'keeps about 364 of 680 paid registrations'.

issues.where: budget 'Measurement stack' and #2 'Registration and QR check-in run on Luma's free plan'; capacity 'occupancy counter from entry and exit scans'; #2 budget 'SMS fallback Rs 2,000'
issues.problem: [SHOW-24] confirms that Luma's free plan offers free events, QR check-in and automatic email/SMS/WhatsApp reminders. Nothing confirms free-plan API or webhook access, which the Growth Center, the holdout randomiser and the BSP flows need. Luma's built-in reminders go to every guest, which would contaminate the 15% holdout. There's no evidence of exit scans, custom attribution precedence or college-ID hashing. Luma Plus is $59 a month billed annually, about Rs 59K or a fifth of the budget. DLT SMS needs a Rs 5,900 entity registration plus Rs 5,900 per sender header [SMS-01], which Rs 2,000 can't cover.
issues.fix: Build the pass, QR and check-in (entry scans plus an occupancy count) into the Growth Center on Neon and Vercel, adding 2-3 person-weeks to analytics (offset by the experiment cuts). Use Luma only as a fallback, with all its automatic reminders off. Count occupancy from entry scans plus hourly clicker exit counts, using offline-capable scanning on local Wi-Fi. Drop the SMS fallback, or fund DLT (about Rs 11.8K) from the cut deposit and ladder cells.

issues.where: dashboard_ai_support of #1, #2 and #3 ('which Ghatkesar squads are missing members?', '2 of your 4 haven't confirmed', ambassador disqualification); claim 'only aggregated, non-PII data reaches the free-tier model'
issues.problem: These copilot tasks need person-level rows (squad members, ambassador names, fraud flags based on phone numbers), which contradicts the plan's own 'aggregated, non-PII only' rule. Free-tier prompts are 'used to improve our products' [GEM-06]. For a healthcare-AI interviewer, data handling is a credibility test.
issues.fix: Have the tools return pseudonymous IDs (squad_7f3a, amb_12) and counts only. The model drafts templates with placeholders, and names and phone numbers are merged in on the server after it responds. Alternatively, run the copilot on the paid tier, where prompts aren't used for training [GEM-06] and demo-volume cost is negligible, and say so on Slide 3.

issues.where: Deliverable: exactly 3 slides
issues.problem: The strategy has about 10 funnel stages x 2 cases, 5 ideas x 15 fields, 20 assumptions, 11 deprioritised items and 8 phases. That cannot fit 3 legible slides, there is no appendix, and skeptical reviewers will read the density as hiding weak spots.
issues.fix:
- Slide 1: one base/stretch funnel table, the waterfall, the floor, and 3 load-bearing assumptions.
- Slide 2: one 5-row table (concept, change in base and stretch, Rs, owner-weeks, dates, test, ICE score) plus a double-down/cut box with the Rs 1.52L to Rs 0.55L trade-off.
- Slide 3: one 5-row table (leading indicator; scale, change and stop thresholds; action) plus a strip showing the gate calendar.
Move the full arithmetic, assumptions and sensitivities to a 'Model' page in the Growth Center and cite it on each slide.

issues.where: capacity PEAK LOAD; A16; A19 '~30 event-day volunteers'
issues.problem: Peak entry is based on 2025's daytime profile: 17.6% of day-1 visitors in the busiest hour, peaking at 11:00, with no entries after 17:00. 2027 moves crowd-heavy programming to 4 pm and adds a 7:30 pm pro-nite. At 30-35% in the peak hour, stretch entry is 726-847 an hour, giving 1.4-1.7x headroom on 1,200 an hour, not 2.8x. Thirty volunteers can't staff 4 lanes, the exception desk, a squad lane, exit counts, shuttle marshalling and 3 halls.
issues.fix: State an evening-weighted arrival assumption (30% in the peak hour). Add 2 surge lanes from 5 to 8 pm. Plan about 60 event-day volunteers across 2 shifts.

issues.where: capacity PERMIT and HARD CAPS
issues.problem: 5,000 is treated as a peak concurrent figure, but CPPMS applications usually state expected attendance. Read as daily footfall, the worst case is 4,500 x 0.9 x 0.75 + 300 + 1,200 = 4,538, which is 91% of the permit.
issues.fix: Check on the CPPMS form whether the figure is concurrent or daily. If daily, apply for 6,000 daily and 5,000 concurrent, and state both figures on Slide 1.

issues.where: Phase 0 'Recruit 60 ambassadors (non-partner colleges only)'; #3 timeline 1-20 Dec; MoUs until 31 Jan
issues.problem: Ambassadors are recruited from 'non-partner' colleges before the partner list exists, so colleges that sign later will break the rule that ambassadors stay out of partner colleges.
issues.fix: Freeze the 60-college partner shortlist by Sun 6 Dec and recruit ambassadors only outside it. If an ambassador's college signs, make that ambassador its club-charter lead and credit their work to #1.

issues.where: #3 concept (a)(b); timeline 'Rewards paid 15-25 Mar'; budget 'Rs 25K squad-completion rewards'
issues.problem: Fast-lane entry is 'unlocked' by the whole squad's verified check-in, which is circular because the lane is how they check in. Ambassador guest passes and pro-nite pit access can't be granted after the event. It's unclear whether the Rs 100 food combo is per squad or per member.
issues.fix: Give fast-lane entry to squads whose members have all reconfirmed by T-1. Unlock front-zone access and the food combo live, once every member has scanned in. Grant event-access perks at T-1 based on reconfirmed recruits, and pay merch, cash and letters after the event on verified check-ins. State 'Rs 100 per squad'.

issues.where: overlap_adjustment (2) precedence; #1 KPI '>=4.0 coded registrations per active partner-week' and operating target (240 partner-weeks); #4 geo-fence on the partner corridors
issues.problem: Competition codes outrank partner codes, and CTWA is geo-fenced to the partner corridors, so the grid's and paid's KPIs move with the precedence rules rather than with performance. The 240 partner-weeks include the 1-7 Feb pause week, so only 220 are effective, which needs 4.36 per partner-week. The 'active partners per week: 40' KPI cannot hold that week.
issues.fix: Measure the grid as all registrations from partner-college students, whatever their code, per partner-week, and judge paid on its geo test. Restate the target as 4.4 over 220 effective partner-weeks. Exempt 1-7 Feb from the 'active partner' and 'days since last registration' alerts.

issues.where: framework ALLOCATION RULE ('budget follows marginal CPV'); organic Rs 14K to 10K; community Rs 16K to 15K
issues.problem: On the model's own curves, organic's marginal CPV between Rs 10K and 14K is Rs 147-179, and community's at Rs 15K is Rs 157. Both beat the grid's marginal of about Rs 196 (before the engine). So the Rs 5K cut gives up about 31 visitors to buy about 26 in the grid, which breaks the stated rule.
issues.fix: Restore organic to Rs 14K and community to Rs 16K, paid for by the bus cut. Otherwise state a non-CPV reason (for example, first-touch over-credit) and build the same discount into the curve.

issues.where: framework scores, #2 'Ease 9'
issues.problem: Ease 9 is defined as 'Rs 20K or less, one owner, configuration only'. The engine has 2 owners (9 person-weeks), a custom switch/transfer/release flow, waitlist operations, a payment gateway for the deposit and 5 tests. That matches Ease 7.
issues.fix: Score Ease 7, giving ICE 6.67. #2 stays ranked second with no tie-break, so delete the 'tie broken by absolute impact' sentence. If the release and waitlist modules are cut, Ease 8 is defensible.

issues.where: north_star; stretch funnel; overlap (5) CEILINGS
issues.problem: [SHOW-02]'s 82% is the median for large paid events; large free events median 76%. Calling 82% a 'ceiling' for a free fest misstates the source, and the base's 78.5% is already above the free-event median.
issues.fix: Write: 'The free large-event median is 76% [SHOW-02]. The base's 78.5% exceeds it through the measured channel mix (72.7%) plus the engine. The stretch is capped at the paid-event median (82%) as an upper bound.'

issues.where: A3; stretch what_must_be_true #1 (x1.10 stall recovery)
issues.problem: In weeks 11-14 of 2025, partnerships ran at 64-97 registrations a week, well above the weeks 6-7 run-rate of about 26. Part of the 'lost 49' was likely deferred, not lost, so crediting a x1.10 recovery may count volume the channel recaptured anyway.
issues.fix: Describe x1.10 as 'up to' and show a stretch variant at x1.045 only: about -81 registrations and -61 visitors.

issues.where: headline 'Two methods agree within 2.3%'; base arithmetic CROSS-CHECK
issues.problem: Method B reuses the conversion layer, haircuts, competitions, reserve and walk-ins, and changes only the acquisition curves. Its agreement with Method A is not independent evidence.
issues.fix: Reword to: 'An alternative acquisition model (step-CPR, no efficiency gains) gives 2,654 (-2.3%).' Present the floor (2,141) as the robustness check.

issues.where: Phase 1 'Competition sponsor go/no-go Fri 15 Jan'; #2 'January club workshops ... reminder test'; T-2 on Thu 11 Mar
issues.problem: 15 Jan is Sankranti, inside the plan's own 13-17 Jan quiet window [fest HYD-21, cal HYD-06]. Reminder tests can't use WhatsApp templates before their 10 Jan approval or during the break, so the January test bed is really 18-29 Jan, which overlaps the mid-terms of autonomous colleges such as NRCM (25-30 Jan) [cal HYD-03].
issues.fix: Move the sponsor go/no-go to Tue 12 Jan. Run the workshop reminder test 19-23 Jan at non-autonomous colleges and label it directional. Make T-2 conditional on the Eid moon sighting.

issues.where: #5 prelims 15-26 Feb; #1 club pre-events 8-27 Feb; P2 degree-college partners
issues.problem: Inter theory exams start 24 Feb [cal HYD-08]. Degree and junior colleges used as exam centres usually restrict gatherings, which affects prelims on 24-26 Feb and pre-events at OU-area partners.
issues.fix: Find out which partner campuses are Inter exam centres. Finish prelims and on-campus pre-events there by 23 Feb, and run later activations off campus.

issues.where: big_idea first sentence; headline_numbers[0]; deprioritised 'Raising the budget' reason
issues.problem: 'Yes, this is Challenge A' and 'Yes, Challenge A' are chat replies, not slide copy. 'No marginal Rs 18-19 per stretch visitor is claimed' refers to an internal draft the reviewers never saw.
issues.fix: Open with: 'Challenge A, Attendee Growth: maximise unique verified external visitors, Hyderabad, 13-14 Mar 2027.' Delete the Rs 18-19 sentence. Confirm 'Challenge A' to the user in chat, not on a slide.

issues.where: stretch funnel 'Walk-ins and day-2 friend passes'; #3 (c); #2 budget
issues.problem: People who use the day-1 friend link register before arriving, so they are registrants, not walk-ins. Grouping them as walk-ins muddles both the 300-a-day walk-in cap and the 6.5% comparison with 2025. The 6 pm link is a marketing-category message: about 1,900-2,400 sends at about Rs 1.14 each with BSP fee and GST, so Rs 2.2-2.8K that isn't budgeted.
issues.fix: Book these people as a 'day-2 friend link' source with their own show rate. Apply the 300-a-day cap to gate registrations only. Add about Rs 2.5K for the send, funded by cutting the Rs 2,600 deposit cell.

issues.where: #2 (e) 'opt-in Rs 99 refundable priority pass returned as food credit'
issues.problem: A deposit returned as food credit is a prepaid voucher, not a refund. Calling it 'refundable' misleads registrants and muddies the ticketed/non-ticketed decision.
issues.fix: Either refund it by UPI at check-in, or call it a 'Rs 99 food-credit priority pass'. Preferably cut the cell to save team bandwidth.

issues.where: deprioritised 'Paid stalls or sponsorships at other colleges' fests'
issues.problem: 'No verified-attendance path' is wrong: a stall can hand out a unique QR or code like any other channel. The real reasons are cost (Rs 15K-2L each [PART-01]) and audience overlap with flagship campuses.
issues.fix: Reword: 'A Rs 15K stall would need at least 77 incremental verified visitors to match the grid's marginal CPV of about Rs 196, at fests whose crowds overlap campuses we treat as credibility partners. Rejected, but we'll accept a free, code-tracked barter booth where one is offered.'
